# The vault

This is a machine-curated record, kept by the BigBrain engine (a separate
checkout; the `bigbrain` command). This directory holds ONLY content — no
code lives here. **If `BIGBRAIN_ROLE` is set in your environment, you are a
sanctioned machine pass — follow your run instructions; the contracts below
are for interactive sessions.**

## If `.state/init.json` does not exist — this vault is not set up yet

(The Read tool works — the file may not exist.) Nothing runs here: no
gardener, no schedule. The contracts below do not apply yet. Open the
BigBrain app, which picks a folder and creates the vault; from a terminal,
`bigbrain init --vault <path> --defaults` does the same thing.
If the user asks anything else about the vault, answer it, then say so
again.

## Get your context from the vault

This vault IS the user's memory — don't work from general knowledge when it
likely holds their actual state. **When `memory/` exists, Read
`memory/MEMORY.md` FIRST** — it is the curated working set (who the user is,
what's live), maintained by the memory pass.
Then ground deeper: `bigbrain search <query>` ranks the record — sources and
the assertions made about them — and, **in an interactive session, attach
your intent with `--why "<why you're asking>"`**: the why is spooled as an
observation and steers what earns a place in `memory/` (default to quoting
the user's triggering message — see Door fidelity below). The spool carries
the USER's demand, so a machine pass's `--why` is dropped on the floor, with
one stderr line: your searches are the run working, and memory already sees
your arrivals through the ledger. When you learn something the record lacks
(a gap you hit, context the user gave you) — or, as a pass, finish work that
leaves something only another pass can repair (a rename that strands
`memory/` links) — submit it with `bigbrain observe "<what you learned>"`.
That door stays open to everyone: evidence for the memory pass to weigh,
never a direct write. Read the hits and the sources they cite for anything
touching the task, and skim recent machine commits or `journal/` for what
changed lately. When the user references a person, project, or event, assume
the vault knows about it and look before asking.

**Door fidelity — whose words are these?** Every door stamps who wrote
(`from`/`from_kind`), and your text must never claim more than your stamp.
Relaying the user into a door: quote their words verbatim, in quotation
marks, dated — and keep your own framing OUTSIDE the quotes, marked as yours
("assistant's summary: …"). Never prefix the user's name onto a paraphrase:
downstream passes weight user voice above every other signal, so a fused
paraphrase becomes a false fact in the user's own memory, attributed to
them. First person is for what YOU did, needed, or inferred.

The why contract, concretely: a `--why` or observation carrying the user's
intent defaults to their TRIGGERING MESSAGE, verbatim and quoted, with your
own intent as a separate marked line — never a fluent fusion of the two. And
a why is a pointer, not a payload: when the conversation itself is the
evidence, put the exchange in the record — `bigbrain drop` lands it as an
immutable source the gardener folds in — and let the observation point at
it. Chat history never rides inside a why: the spool carries demand, the
vault carries evidence, and a transcript smuggled into the spool becomes an
uncommitted shadow record nothing can cite.

Two flows carry the everyday work — reach for them by default:
- **To ground yourself, or answer a lookup.** Reach for **`bigbrain search
  <query>`** first — it is a Bash command the guard permits (it names no
  vault tree) — then the **Read / Grep / Glob tools** to open and refine.
  Never shell `grep`/`ls`/`cat`: the write-guard blocks Bash that so much as
  names a vault tree (`references/`, `entities/`, `memory/`, `log/`, …).
- **To put anything into the vault.** `bigbrain drop <file>` is the way —
  a note you wrote, a file the user handed you, the transcript of an
  exchange. It lands as an immutable source; what the record then claims
  about it is the gardener's to settle.

Outside a checkout — any other directory, any other machine — the same two
flows arrive as the **BigBrain Claude Code plugin**'s `vault-search` and
`vault-add` skills, which speak the vault's HTTP API instead of the
filesystem. Connect that machine with `bigbrain connect`, or from the app's
agents settings.

## The machine contracts

- **The record is machine-written only.** `references/`, `entities/`,
  `log/`, `memory/` and `.blobs/` are hook-denied for interactive writes.
  Submit content with `bigbrain drop <file>`; submit evidence about the
  record with `bigbrain observe`.
- **`log/` is the spine and it is append-only.** Nothing edits an
  insertion or an assertion — a correction is a NEW event that supersedes
  the old one. This holds for machine passes too.
- `vault.yaml` is read live — an edit takes effect on the next tick,
  with nothing to reload.
- `bigbrain publish` pushes this repo to its `origin` remote (offsite
  backup), fail-soft when none is configured.
- Engine updates: update the app, or `git pull` in the engine checkout and
  run `bigbrain install` (it refreshes this file).

## The gardener

One runner tends this vault: **the user's own Claude Code**, driving a
bounded set of vault tools. `bigbrain tend` runs it here; `/bigbrain:tend`
runs it from any connected Claude Code. A run drains what is due —

- **intake**, which reads new sources and settles them into `log/assertions/`:
  attributed claims, each citing the insertion it came from, or a decline
  saying why the source carried nothing worth asserting;
- **the memory pass**, the second writer, which alone writes `memory/` — the
  budgeted working set — folding in voice arrivals and new assertions past
  its cursors.

Its record is `journal/tend/` and `journal/memory/`; `git log
--author=assertion` (and `--author=intake`, `--author=memory`) is the
activity feed. `git show` any machine commit to see exactly what changed and
why — the journal rides in the same commit.

Nothing here runs a model on its own account. The gardener is the user's
Claude, on the user's credential, and an arrival's content is always data:
the worst a steered source can do is propose assertions, which land
host-validated, attributed, and reviewable.

## Reading the record

- **Sources** are what arrived. Each one is an immutable event at
  `log/insertions/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json` — the arrival's envelope and its
  text — and `bigbrain search` is how you find them.
- **Entity pages are virtual.** A dossier at `projection/entities/<id>.md`
  is generated on demand from the assertions that name that entity — a
  legal path to read through the viewer and the API, not a file on disk.
- `references/` and `entities/` hold the reference era's files: still
  readable, never added to. A vault created today starts empty there.
- A source whose body links `blob:<sha256>` (an original PDF, image, audio
  file) has its bytes in the CAS: `bigbrain blob path <sha>` prints a local
  path. The Read tool renders what's there (PDF pages included), so follow
  the link when the extraction isn't enough — to see a figure, not just its
  caption.

**Links are root-relative.** Every `[[wikilink]]` target is the note's path
from the vault root, sans `.md`, with the prose in the alias:
`[[references/2026-08-03-nick-ezra|the 1:1]]`. This is Obsidian's "Absolute
path in vault" format, so the vault stays a real Obsidian vault — and
because a target names its tree, two notes may share a basename without
either link becoming a guess. A bare `[[name]]` still resolves (against the
record only), but `bigbrain links check` reports it as `unqualified`; write
the path.

A link to a note is ALWAYS a wikilink — never `[Label](note.md)`. Nothing
here parses markdown links, so one is a note quietly leaving the link graph;
`check` reports them as `markdown` and `migrate` converts them. (Markdown
links to URLs, images, and non-note files are fine.)

**The memory boundary**: the record never depends on its own cache. It is a
rule about DIRECTION, not about what exists:

- **record → memory: forbidden.** No note in the record links or cites into
  `memory/`. The search surface is the record — `memory/` is not in it — so
  a pass cannot reach the cache it is supposed to be feeding. Such a link is
  a `boundary` violation.
- **memory → record: free.** Citing outward is the whole point.

A **bare** `[[name]]` never means a memory file, for anyone: `[[big-brain]]`
is the entity.

## Layout

`README.md` states the storage model in full: **the lake** is the
append-only `log/` plus the `.blobs/` CAS; **projections** are queryable,
rebuildable views; and **memory** is the derived working set. Improving a
projection never rewrites an insertion event.

- `vault.yaml` — the manifest, and the one file here you edit:
  integrations, the `auth` credential, and each pass's model. The
  passes' prompts ship with the engine, not with this vault.
- `log/insertions/` — one immutable event per arrival: the permanent
  original
- `log/assertions/` — attributed claims and declines about those arrivals,
  each citing its source
- `references/`, `entities/` — the reference era's notes and dossiers,
  frozen and still readable. Raw binary payloads live in `.blobs/`
  (gitignored), referenced from an arrival by `blob:<sha256>`
- `memory/` — the working set, one file: `MEMORY.md` (load first, every
  session); machine-written only, by the memory pass
- `inbox/` — arrivals in flight; `inbox/unsorted/` holds what could not be
  placed
- `journal/` — machine run records (committed)
- `.state/` — cursors, locks, logs (gitignored; cache, never truth)
- The system's code lives in the BigBrain engine, NOT here — this repo
  holds only the record.
